message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated American composers across different eras and styles:

| Composer | Lifespan | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|----------|--------------------------------|
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854–1932) | “March King” – iconic marches like *The Stars and Stripes Forever* |
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | Blended jazz & classical; *Rhapsody in Blue*, *Porgy and Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | “American Sound”; *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | Broadway & symphonic genius; *West Side Story*, *Candide* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910–1981) | Modernist with lyrical touch; *Adagio for Strings* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism pioneer; *Einstein on the Beach*, film scores |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Contemporary minimalism; *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalist innovator; *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | Early modernist; *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **William Grant Still** (1895–1978) | First African‑American composer to have a symphony performed by a major orchestra |

These figures span from the late 19th century to contemporary times and represent a broad spectrum of American musical innovation—from patriotic marches to avant‑garde minimalism.
